opening.headline: This addresses how to block quality degradation in the pipeline before it impacts operations when changing prompts.
body: Changing just one line of the prompt doesn't mean quality degradation isn't noticed—teams focusing solely on average metrics often detect such issues late. If there had been a checkpoint before deployment to re-evaluate quality using the same input, the rollout itself would have been halted.

In this class, we first learn the components of evaluation—eval case, inference, trace, metric, and scorer—and then examine an evaluation gate that automatically runs evaluations in CI to prevent promotion when evaluation criteria are not met. We continue by verifying gradual rollout and quality alerts after passing evaluation.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the automation of evaluation gate and scorer
It is possible to determine whether the design that prevents promotion upon evaluation failure is appropriate.

screens.title: Quality plummeted for some customers after changing prompts
screens.lead: Consider, after reading about a scenario where a one-line prompt modification is deployed directly into operations, at what point could you have stopped it.

visual.alt: A diagram comparing pipelines that are deployed directly into operation without any gateways, and pipelines that have evaluation gates.
labels: Promotion will be suspended if standards are not met.

paragraphs: A team modified the system prompt for a customer service agent by just one line, making only a minor adjustment to the wording. They lightly reviewed it and deployed it directly into operations without further changes. A few days later, inquiries were received indicating a significant drop in response quality among a specific customer group.

The team detected the anomaly late because they were monitoring the overall average score. The affected customer group represented only a portion of the total traffic, and the decline was nearly hidden within the average.

What if there was a checkpoint before deployment that retested quality using the same input bundle? At the moment the revised prompt fails to meet the standard, the promotion itself would have halted, and customers would not have encountered the issue.

This course covers how to make evaluation distribution pipelines a gateway process. It examines sequentially how evaluations are structured, how they are automatically executed, and what actions are required after a student passes.

callout.label: Note
callout.text: The terminology for evaluation components used in this class is based on the agent evaluation documentation of the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. Similar concepts exist on other platforms under different names.

screens.title: Has an assessment been included in the deployment pipeline?
screens.lead: Imagine our team's deployment flow in your mind. You don't need to enter an answer, simply select a question and the instructor's summary will unfold.

items.prompt: At which stage of the pipeline is the evaluation currently?
items.answer: If evaluation is only occasionally run on a developer's laptop for verification, then the deployment pipeline has no evaluation. The statement that something is in the pipeline means that whenever a change is pushed, it is automatically executed against a predefined dataset, and the results determine whether it proceeds to the next stage.

items.prompt: What would stop if it fails to pass?
items.answer: If evaluation results are recorded but nothing stops, it is merely a report, not a gate. When criteria are not met, the action to proceed to the next environment must not occur. The key issue is whether this halt occurs due to human memory or pipeline rules.

items.prompt: How does evaluation during development differ from evaluation at deployment?
items.answer: During development, we frequently run lightweight evaluations to quickly verify changes to prompts or models. The evaluations run upon each deployment are regression checks that confirm the system maintains previous quality using a fixed dataset. The two types of evaluations have different objectives, hence they differ in dataset size and execution frequency.

screens.outro: Now let's examine one by one how the evaluation is carried out.

screens.title: Evaluation components: from eval case to scorer results
screens.lead: When a card is selected, it flips to show an explanation. Learn the terms in the order of evaluation by navigating to the next card with the right arrow.

visual.alt: This is a set of icons illustrating the evaluation flow from inference, trace, metric, to analysis in an eval case.

cards.back: This specification outlines what an agent should do. It can capture not only a single question but also multi-turn conversational phases, the agent's current state—i.e., the conversation context—and how the agent simulates user responses during reasoning. Evaluation begins with this specification, so the reliability of evaluation increases the more closely the eval cases resemble actual usage patterns.

This is the step of actually executing an evaluation case. If a conversation plan is present, it simulates the user's responses and inserts them during execution. That is, this stage generates actual behavior by feeding the agent evaluation-level inputs, and only after this stage is complete does a target for evaluation emerge.

After reasoning is complete, the remaining record is of agent actions. It includes model inputs, responses, and tool calls, and preserves facts without any alterations. Evaluation is based on this record, so all evidence of evaluation is contained within the trace. Traces captured from operational traffic can also be evaluated using the same method.

This is the scoring value computed per trace. Methods that require a reference answer, such as Exact Match, are referred to as reference-based, while methods that judge based solely on the trace, such as Helpfulness, are called reference-free. Reference-free methods are used for open-ended questions where preparing a reference answer is difficult.

An automated grader that calculates metric values. It can use predefined items such as Task Success, Safety, or custom-defined metrics. By analyzing grader results, one can identify clusters of failures and link them to test cases, which in turn can serve as evidence for prompt or tool improvement recommendations.

screens.outro: Now that we know the component, we'll look at the approach of automatically placing this evaluation in the pipeline as a gate each time.

screens.title: CI Automation and Promotion Hold Flow
screens.lead: Toggle the switch to compare how the same change flows through a pipeline with and without an evaluation gate.

visual.alt: This is a flow where evaluation is automatically executed after each change in CI, and promotion is blocked if the evaluation does not meet the baseline.
labels: Check for issues after operation and perform rollback

states.label: No gate: Evaluation is for reference only
states.body: Even if evaluations are performed, the results are only recorded and are not linked to promotion rules. The structure assumes that developers will automatically halt deployments upon seeing the results, but during busy periods, they may skip checking the results altogether. If evaluation is limited to occasional activities during development, the same changes may be deployed to production without any modifications, and the issue only surfaces through customer inquiries. In such cases, rollback becomes a post-incident remedial measure.

states.label: Gate exists: rules prevent promotion
states.body: Evaluation is divided into three types. Rapid Evaluation, which frequently checks newly developed logic or model changes, Test Case Evaluation, which regularly verifies regression against a specific dataset within CI/CD pipelines, and Online Monitoring, which continuously ensures operational quality. Among these, Test Case Evaluation automatically runs and records evaluation scores every time CI changes, and pipeline rules are implemented to prevent promotion if the evaluation falls below the threshold—this is known as the evaluation gate. If issues are identified after promotion, the system rolls back to the previous version. In summary, CI handles execution, the baseline handles judgment, and pipeline rules handle halting.

screens.outro: Just passing through the gate does not mean the end. In the following explanation, we will examine the deployment methods after passage.

screens.title: Reasons for gradual deployment even after passing evaluation
screens.lead: The instructor explains step by step why approved changes are not immediately deployed across the entire system. Click the following arrow to proceed step by step.

steps.title: Limitations of the Preliminary Assessment Scope
steps.body: Pre-evaluation checks quality only within the scope of the prepared eval cases. Even if synthetic scenarios are created through simulation, it's difficult to fully capture the actual user input—including tone, length, and request types. Therefore, passing evaluation means exceeding the criteria within the prepared inputs, but does not imply safety across all possible inputs.

steps.title: Quality drift occurring in operations
steps.body: In operations, user behavior or external data may change gradually, leading to a slow degradation in quality. This phenomenon is known as quality drift—i.e., the observed decline in agent performance over time. Even if the model remains unchanged, quality drift can occur due to shifts in actual user behavior or subtle changes in prompt chain interactions, making it impossible to detect based solely on evaluation at deployment time.

steps.title: Export first with light traffic
steps.body: Therefore, the new version is initially enabled for only a portion of traffic, and the Online Monitor asynchronously evaluates the trace of actual traffic. If issues arise, they affect only a small number of users, and the rollout ratio is expanded only when no anomalies are detected. Compared to enabling it for all customers at once, the potential impact of incidents is significantly reduced.

steps.title: How the Online Monitor operates
steps.body: Online Monitor assists with scheduled evaluation loops approximately every 10 minutes. First, it retrieves samples from Cloud Trace and Cloud Logging based on the configured filter. Second, it calculates the configured metrics using the evaluation service. Third, it logs the results in Cloud Logging and exports the numeric score to Cloud Monitoring. You can adjust evaluation costs by specifying the sampling ratio and the maximum number of samples per execution. For monitoring to work, an agent must export OpenTelemetry signals.

steps.title: If a problem is observed, stop zooming and rollback.
steps.body: If monitoring detects a quality degradation, pause scaling and roll back to a previous version, limiting the impact to a small number of users. This creates a structure where the limitations of pre-release evaluation are supplemented by ongoing monitoring in production. With the combination of pre-gate, gradual rollout, continuous evaluation, and rollback, quality degradation can be detected early and resolved with minimal impact.

screens.outro: Now we will examine how the result of continuous evaluation is read from the configuration file to trigger an alarm.

screens.title: Define the rollback point by quality alert
screens.lead: Review the configuration file for Cloud Monitoring alert policies. Line-by-line explanations describe what each value sets and the symptoms that arise if it is misconfigured.

data.code:
displayName: "Low Task Success Score"
conditions:
- displayName: "Task Success < 0.8"
  conditionThreshold:
    filter: >
      metric.type="aiplatform.googleapis.com/online_evaluator/scores"
      AND metric.labels.evaluation_metric_name="task_success"
    comparison: COMPARISON_LT
    thresholdValue: 0.8
    duration: 1800s
    aggregations:
    - alignmentPeriod: 60s
      perSeriesAligner: ALIGN_MEAN
combiner: OR
enabled: true
notificationChannels:
- "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/notificationChannels/CHANNEL_ID"

notes.note: Among the evaluation scoring metrics exported from Online Monitor to Cloud Monitoring, only the task_success metric is selected. If the filter is misconfigured, the metric will not be captured, and thus alarms will not be triggered even if the quality is poor.

The condition is satisfied when the average Task Success is below 0.8 and this state persists for 1800 seconds, i.e., 30 minutes. If the period is set too short, alerts will be triggered by temporary fluctuations; if set too long, quality degradation will be detected too late. This threshold is set with a similar sensitivity to that of the evaluation gate's threshold.

It calculates values every 60 seconds and computes an average. Using a different method instead of averaging can change how sharply some customers' declines are obscured. By separately maintaining indicators broken down by customer segment, you can also observe the downturns that would otherwise be obscured by the overall average.

The conditions are combined using an OR logic and trigger if any one condition is satisfied, then an alert is sent through the notification channel. Alerts only notify; they do not initiate upgrades or rollbacks. Whether a rollback occurs is determined by the pipeline rules and the operator's judgment. If the notification channel is disabled, checks are still performed, but no notification is sent to users—confirmation can only be obtained via the Monitoring's Alerting page.

screens.outro: By aligning the alert criteria with gate criteria, you can maintain the same quality perception throughout both pre-deployment and post-deployment phases.

screens.title: Key points and reflection
screens.lead: This is a screen that organizes the evaluation gate and automation workflow. Read it slowly and try to apply it to our pipeline.

paragraphs: The evaluation process follows a flow wherein eval cases are defined, inference is executed, traces are recorded, a scorer computes the metric, and the results are analyzed for improvement. Each component has a clearly defined role, making it easy to identify where errors occur.

If evaluation fails, promotion should not occur. This halt can be referred to as a gate when it occurs based on pipeline rules rather than human memory. CI automation repeatedly enforces this gate by evaluating test cases for every change.
After passing evaluation, gradual rollout is performed and monitored online. Inputs outside of the evaluation cases and quality drift over time are not captured by pre-evaluation.

Alerts are notifications; decisions regarding promotion and rollback are left to the pipeline rules and the responsible party. Alert thresholds should be set with the same sensitivity as gate baselines. Additionally, do not look only at the overall average—break down by customer segment or slice to avoid masking partial declines.

Finally, let us return to the introductory example of this course. A single prompt modification undergoes test case evaluation, is compared against a benchmark, and if it falls short of the standard, promotion is halted. Even if it passes, it initially opens only with a small traffic volume, allowing the Online Monitor to observe actual traces. The design objective of the evaluation gate is to ensure that if one layer is missed, another layer catches it.

callout.label: A sentence to remember
callout.text: Promotion does not occur if the evaluation fails. Additionally, even after passing, it is re-verified during operations.

checks.q: Pair the evaluation criteria with their descriptions.
right: Execution log containing model input, response, and tool calls
Specifications defining what the agent should do and the expected outcomes
An automated grader that calculates results for each trace
Execution of the actual eval case
checks.explain: When executing an eval case using inference, traces are recorded, and the scorer calculates a metric value for each trace.
checks.intro: Pair the evaluation components with their roles. Results are not recorded.
checks.correctFeedback: Yes, correct. When executed, records are generated and an automated grader evaluates those records.
checks.incorrectFeedback: The specifications, execution, logging, and scoring components are out of alignment. Please review the order in which they are placed within the evaluation flow.

checks.q: For the evaluation gate to function meaningfully, how should promotion blocking be implemented?
options: The operator sees the result, remembers it, and halts the deployment.
If the threshold is not met, the pipeline rule does not perform the promotion action itself.
Evaluation is occasionally run during development and omitted when deploying.
After promotion, check the results when issues are observed.
checks.explain: Blocking should occur based on pipeline rules, not on human memory, and the CI automation evaluates the test cases every time a change is made to ensure this gate is passed.

wrong.0: Dependence on humans can lead to potential omissions.
wrong.2: An automated evaluation gate runs every deployment.
wrong.3: Upgrade post-checking corresponds to a post-rollback and is not a gate.

checks.intro: Choose the conditions under which the evaluation gate operates meaningfully. The results are not recorded.
checks.correctFeedback: Yes. Blocking must occur according to rules in order to be consistently enforced each time.
checks.incorrectFeedback: This approach fails or operates late. Recall that a gateway should not rely on anyone's memory.

checks.q: When the quality alarm of Online Monitor triggers, who decides whether to perform a rollback?
options: The system automatically rolls back immediately when an alarm sounds.
Online Monitor stops the evaluation and reverses the promotion.
Cloud Monitoring automatically redeploys the previous version.
Alerts are merely notifications, and decisions are made based on pipeline rules and the operator's judgment.
checks.explain: Alerts are the result of an alert policy, and promotion or rollback decisions are made based on pipeline rules and the responsible party. Therefore, alert thresholds are set to align with gate thresholds.

wrong.0: Alarms themselves do not include rollback actions.
wrong.1: The monitor evaluates and records samples but does not revert promotions.
wrong.2: Re-distribution is not a warning but the responsibility of the pipeline and the assigned personnel.

checks.intro: After the quality alarm sounds, choose who decides on the rollback. The result is not recorded.
checks.correctFeedback: Yes. Alerts are raised, but decisions are made according to rules and human judgment.
checks.incorrectFeedback: The alarm itself has no rollback operation. Please reconsider the roles of alarms, promotion, and rollback separately.

glossary.def: This is a pipeline checkpoint that prevents advancement to the next stage if the evaluation results do not meet the criteria.
An automated grader that calculates scoring values for tracing or output, either using built-in items or defining them directly.
This is a method that automatically executes evaluations and retains the results every time a change occurs.
This rule prevents the action of moving to the following environment when the evaluation fails.
The phenomenon where agent quality degrades over time due to user behavior or data changes.

misconceptions.myth: Once evaluated, it is safe to operate.
misconceptions.fact: Pre-release evaluation is verified only within the prepared eval cases. Any input outside of these cases and time-dependent quality drift must be monitored during operations.

misconceptions.myth: Looking at only the overall average score is enough to understand the quality.
misconceptions.fact: If customer segments or slices are not separated, the decline of certain groups is absorbed into the average.

misconceptions.myth: The evaluation gate is a procedure where a person visually verifies the results before deployment.
misconceptions.fact: Pipeline rules must automatically disable promotion actions when standards are not met to ensure consistent compliance every time.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: Evaluation consists of eval case, execution, trace, scoring, and analysis flow.
The evaluation gate prevents promotion when benchmarks are not met, and CI automation executes it each time it is modified.
We continue to verify quality drift through gradual rollout and ongoing evaluation after approval.
Alarms and rollback criteria are aligned with gateway criteria.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for your own reflection only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: Where does our deployment pipeline actually stop when quality scores are low?
